name: Rilpivirine
route_note: oral tablet once daily with a meal; long-acting IM injection monthly or every 2 months with cabotegravir

discovery.note: Flexible diarylpyrimidine designed to bind the NNRTI pocket in several conformations, retaining activity against some resistant strains.

tagline: Low-dose NNRTI in single tablets and in the first long-acting injectable HIV regimen
summary: Rilpivirine is a second-generation non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor taken orally once daily with food or given as a long-acting intramuscular injection. Combined with cabotegravir, it forms the first complete long-acting injectable HIV treatment, given monthly or every two months. Oral absorption requires stomach acid, so proton-pump inhibitors are contraindicated.
mechanism: Rilpivirine binds the allosteric NNRTI pocket of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase and blocks DNA synthesis non-competitively. Its flexible structure lets it adapt to mutations in the pocket, so it keeps activity against some K103N viruses.

Resistance mutations such as E138K and Y181C reduce susceptibility and give cross-resistance with other NNRTIs. The long-acting injection is a nanosuspension that releases drug slowly from muscle over weeks.
uses: HIV-1 infection in treatment-naive patients with viral load at or below 100,000 copies/mL (oral, in combination)
Switch therapy in virologically suppressed patients (Odefsey, Juluca)
Long-acting injectable maintenance therapy with cabotegravir in suppressed patients

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Edurant is approved in May 2011, followed by the single tablet Complera (with emtricitabine and tenofovir disoproxil) in August.

history.title: Juluca
history.detail: Dolutegravir/rilpivirine becomes the first two-drug complete regimen approved for HIV maintenance.

history.title: EU long-acting approval
history.detail: The EU approves Rekambys injection with cabotegravir (Vocabria) in December 2020.

history.title: Cabenuva
history.detail: The FDA approves monthly cabotegravir/rilpivirine injections in January 2021, and every-2-month dosing in 2022.

pk.half_life: oral about 45–50 h; long-acting injection apparent half-life of months
pk.bioavailability: must be taken with a meal; absorption depends on stomach acid

facts: Proton-pump inhibitors are contraindicated with oral rilpivirine because they reduce its absorption.
Cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was the first long-acting injectable regimen for HIV treatment.
